items.defectStatement: findMembers unconditionally applies every response, allowing an older request that finishes last to overwrite the latest page or membership refresh.
obligations: Only the latest member request for a model may update its members and pagination metadata.
Distinguish overlapping requests even when they request the same offset.
Preserve member conversion to Discourse.User and the returned promise.
items.notes: Callback identity supplies a per-request token within the exact anchor. Comparing offsets alone misses same-page refresh races. The replacement passed simulated out-of-order navigation and refresh checks.

items.defectStatement: Admin::GroupsController#create ignores the submitted alias_level, so newly created groups retain the default instead of the administrator's selection.
obligations: Assign a supplied alias_level before saving, using the same conversion as update.
Preserve the default when alias_level is absent or blank.
Preserve name trimming, visibility handling, and save response behavior.
items.exampleFix:
group = Group.new
    group.name = (params[:name] || '').strip
    group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"
    group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i if params[:alias_level].present?

    if group.save
items.notes: The update action supplies the required assignment pattern.

items.defectStatement: The Next action permits offset == user_count, requesting an empty page when the count is an exact multiple of the page size. The incorrect totalPages calculation also prevents showingLast from blocking that navigation.
obligations: Prevent Next from advancing beyond the last valid page start.
Preserve normal advancement to full and partially filled pages.
Keep the offset nonnegative for empty groups.
items.notes: Using the existing totalPages value would retain the bug. This local fix prevents empty-page navigation; correcting the page-count display and disabled styling requires a separate change outside the anchor.

items.defectStatement: remove_member deletes the membership through group.users.delete, bypassing GroupUser destruction callbacks and leaving the group's cached user_count inflated.
obligations: Destroy the matching membership with callbacks so its counter cache is decremented.
Remove only the specified group's membership, preserving the user and other memberships.
Preserve automatic-group protection and response handling.
items.exampleFix:
def remove_member
    group = Group.find(params.require(:group_id).to_i)
    user_id = params.require(:user_id).to_i

    return can_not_modify_automatic if group.automatic

    group.group_users.where(user_id: user_id).destroy_all

    if group.save
      render json: success_json
    else
      render_json_error(group)
    end
  end
items.notes: The finding supplies the association and destruction operation; the repository confirms both. Loading a User and still calling group.users.delete does not address the callback defect.

items.defectStatement: The public members endpoint passes unchecked limit and offset parameters into its query. Oversized limits permit excessive serialization, while negative pagination values can cause database errors.
obligations: Enforce a positive, bounded page size while preserving the default of 50.
Prevent negative offsets from reaching the query.
Report the effective limit and offset in response metadata.
Preserve member ordering and total-count semantics.
items.exampleFix:
limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i
    limit = 50 if limit <= 0
    limit = [limit, 200].min
    offset = [params[:offset].to_i, 0].max

    total = group.users.count
    members = group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)
items.notes: Other reasonable finite caps and explicit validation errors are valid alternatives. An upper bound alone does not handle zero or negative limits.

items.defectStatement: Passing user_id to group.users.delete performs an association-scoped lookup that raises RecordNotFound when the user is no longer a member, causing repeated or concurrent removal requests to fail.
obligations: Treat an already absent membership as a successful no-op.
Continue removing existing memberships without deleting the user.
Preserve automatic-group protection and existing response handling.
items.notes: The finding's claim that integer IDs always cause AssociationTypeMismatch is inaccurate for the pinned Rails version. The relevant failure is the missing associated record. The supplied finding identifies group.remove; its implementation safely destroys matching join records.
